Anarcs Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Anarcs, Hungary

Demolished. Anarcs's Jewish cemetery appears on an 1870 cadastral map, though it was later demolished. The village's first known Jewish resident, stillman Izsák Absolon, arrived around 1740; by 1890 the community numbered 132 (of 987 total residents), though it had shrunk to 63 by 1941. Formally organized at the end of the 19th century under the Kisvárda rabbinate, the community maintained a synagogue, cemetery, cheder, and mikveh. Eight Holocaust survivors returned after the war, though only six Jews remained in Anarcs by 1949.
